name: saasplane
description: The SaaS Plane agent plugin marketplace — three plugins, one per domain and the set is closed. spn-devex installs in every repository; spn-apps acts on the nodes an apps repository declares; spn-infra acts on the estate. A stack or a cloud is a folder inside the plugin that owns its domain, never a plugin of its own.

plugins.name: spn-devex
plugins.description: SaaS Plane devex — installed in every repository, stack-agnostic. Ten skills: the eight stages in order (bootstrap, scm, ideate, develop, test, provision, deliver, operate) plus check and report, which serve any stage. The SPN engineer persona, the spn-panel reviewer and the eleven lens files it convenes. The refs a partner needs without the book: what a plugin is, what a skill is, the workspace and the workstream loop, what a repository declares, the doc-set grammar, block and figure spelling, decision cards, and the templates every page is copied from, each linking one shared stylesheet. Hooks that deny hand-edits to generated files, check every document against the bars the book states mechanically, print the window's orientation at session start, and read a workstream's split plan before a seat write or a close.

plugins.name: spn-apps
plugins.description: SaaS Plane apps domain — one plugin for every APPS repository, stack-agnostic with its stacks inside it. Six skills: new, implement, review, run, verify, release. The apps model a node is built from, the platform model a partner adopts rather than rebuilds — tenancy, identity, surfaces, data and trust, lifecycle, and the seven modules that ship — and the rules a change must obey, with each stack's parser kept apart from the rule it serves.

plugins.name: spn-infra
plugins.description: SaaS Plane infra domain — one plugin for every INFRA repository, cloud-agnostic with its clouds inside it. Six skills reading the same words as apps: new, implement, review, run, verify, release. The estate model — shape, packages, blueprints, resources, apps, modules, trust, operate, ships — the estate laws and the name grammar, and the per-cloud material. A hook that denies secrets, ARNs, account ids, provider strings outside a cloud entry, and hand edits to built output: the rule stated once and cloud-free, the spellings belonging to each cloud.
